answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making each identity stake capital that is slashed on fraud, so spawning a thousand fake agents costs more than any payout they could extract. Like karst limestone, a thin surface hides costly tunnels beneath: every new identity passes slow onboarding at the network's nadir of trust, where checks are strictest. Reputation accrues only through completed, paid work, and a violet flag marks identities too young to hold escrow — so attackers must pay in time and capital before touching real value.
